items.summary: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.
items.title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition

items.summary: EHR2Trace converts local hospital EHR extracts (delimited text and spreadsheets) into OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS. The two targets are derived independently from a single canonical layer rather than one from the other, every published row carries a link back to the source rows it came from, and fifty-five checks encode the properties a conversion must satisfy before it can be used as training data, including the leakage failures that are invisible to schema validation. Where the data does not answer a question, the converter blocks and says so instead of substituting a default. Companion paper: EHR2Trace: Auditable EHR Data Infrastructure for Patient World Models and Clinical Agents (arXiv:2609.38193).
items.title: EHR2Trace: a deterministic converter from local EHR exports to OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS, with row-level lineage

items.summary: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. We propose PRB-WM, a physics-regularized Beta world model for predictive per-subcarrier link adaptation on real time-varying UWA channels. A persistence-anchored stochastic latent-space dynamics model learns how the channel evolves; a counterfactual outcome head evaluates, for every candidate modulation and coding scheme (MCS), a Beta-binomial distribution of bit errors on shared imagined futures; and a chance-constrained receding-horizon model predictive controller maximizes expected spectral efficiency subject to a bounded probability of violating the bit error rate (BER) target. To the best of our knowledge, PRB-WM is the first world model for UWA communications. In closed-loop replay of six measured sea-trial links from the public UWA Channel Library against a 24-method pool spanning the full methodological spectrum, PRB-WM attains a mean goodput 87% above the strongest baseline, ranks first on all six time-varying links at the longest lookahead, and is the only method whose realized frame risk decreases systematically with lookahead, meeting the BER-violation contract where no baseline does. Ablations confirm that rollout sampling dispersion is essential to the chance constraint and that the physics anchor is necessary for trainability.
items.title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels

items.summary: The underwater sound speed distribution directly governs acoustic propagation paths, rendering it critically important for underwater acoustic communication and target localization. Conventional sound speed profile (SSP) prediction methods provide a good way to estimate the underwater sound speed distribution without on-site data measurement, thus breaking through the coverage area constraints of sonar observation equipment and making the model universal in most marine areas. However, underwater sound speed exhibits multi-scale variations, such as diurnal, quarterly, and intermittent fluctuations caused by ocean processes such as internal waves. This makes it difficult for the fixed structure models in existing methods to have good generalization ability for multi-scale sound speed distribution patterns. To tackle this problem, we proposed a lightweight hybrid basis-function empowered Kolmogorov-Arnold network (LHBF-KAN) model for multi-scale sound speed prediction. We aim to construct a multi-branch representation layer in which different basis functions respond to distinct temporal patterns, from slowly varying background trends to rapid fluctuations induced by dynamic ocean processes, allowing the model to naturally accommodate the inherently multi-scale evolution of sound speed at different depths. To prevent the multi-branch structure from increasing model size, a pruning strategy is further introduced to suppress branches with consistently low contribution during training, yielding a compact architecture, suitable for deployment on resource constrained underwater platforms.
items.title: Robust Prediction of Internal Wave-Affected Multi-Scale Sound Speed Distribution Using Lightweight Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with Hybrid Basis Functions

items.summary: Underwater acoustic target detection and recognition are essential to marine surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Despite substantial advances in deep learning, existing systems typically produce binary detection decisions, categorical labels, or scalar confidence scores, offering limited insight into the physical evidence underlying their outputs. Large language models (LLMs) offer an opportunity to move underwater acoustic sensing toward interpretable, evidence-grounded understanding; however, generic audio encoders struggle to capture the distinctive physical characteristics of underwater acoustics, and physically annotated data are scarce. In this paper, the first of a two-part series, we propose a from-signals-to-evidence framework that integrates physics-aware acoustic encoding with a pretrained LLM, organized around a unified feature-evidence-decision chain with a shared reasoning core. An open input layer accommodates heterogeneous information-raw waveforms, time-frequency representations, environmental and geographic data, and textual physical priors-unifying detection and recognition within a common formulation. In Part I, we instantiate this framework for target recognition through an Underwater Acoustic Physics-aware Transformer (UPT), which tokenizes complementary acoustic representations and learns task-disentangled physical representations through four physics-oriented learning tasks. We develop a physics-parameterized data engine that provides traceable supervision at two levels of granularity and introduce an attribute-level evaluation protocol to assess the physical fidelity of generated descriptions. Experiments on simulated recordings of four vessels demonstrate accurate vessel recognition and reliable estimation of shaft frequency, blade-passing frequency, and machinery-related attributes.
items.title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part I: Framework and Recognition

items.summary: The Mathematics of 3D Printing Slicing: STL Geometry, Ray-Casting & Toolpaths is an open-access engineering monograph and interactive instructional module published by the Prep4Uni.Online OER Initiative . This work provides an analytical, undergraduate/postgraduate-level treatment of the computational geometry foundations required to translate three-dimensional surface meshes into layer-by-layer machine toolpaths. Aligned with international accreditation standards—specifically the Washington Accord (WA1–WA5) and EUR-ACE First/Second Cycle frameworks—this publication establishes the mathematical proofs, vector algorithms, and point-in-polygon logic governing modern additive manufacturing slicing software. Core Mathematical & Computational Themes: STL Topology & Facet Representation: Analysis of unstructured triangulated surface meshes, outward unit normal vectors (\(\mathbf{n}\)), vertex coordinate systems, and planar boundary extraction. Parametric Facet-Plane Intersection: Step-by-step vector linear interpolation for deriving the intersection segment \(S_k\) formed by cutting planes at \(z = z_k\), addressing non-manifold edges, vertex touching, and numerical epsilon shifts. Jordan Curve Theorem & Parity Logic: Formal implementation of the 2D Ray-Casting algorithm and Even-Odd Parity test for robust interior, exterior, and internal void classification across arbitrary closed slices. Toolpath Trajectory Generation: Comparative kinematics and geometry between continuous concentric perimeter offset loops and 45° zigzag parallel hatch raster patterns. Formative Assessment Suite: A three-tier verification suite comprising 8 foundational concepts, 7 real-world slicer failure debugging scenarios, and 6 step-by-step quantitative engineering worked examples. Note: The full interactive web edition—featuring client-side HTML5 simulation canvas engines, dynamic parameter sliders, and real-time slice projection mathematics—is accessible at: https://prep4uni.online/stem/physical-technologies/industrial-and-manufacturing-technologies/additive-manufacturing-3d-printing/mathematics-of-slicing/
items.title: The Mathematics of 3D Printing Slicing: STL Geometry, Ray-Casting & Toolpaths

items.summary: NANOROBOTIC CARGO TRANSPORT AND MICROSCALE MANIPULATION INTEGRITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation DOI Fission Research Flagship 02 | Starli Active Nanosystems Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli | Research Atlas v1.0 (October 2026) How can a micro/nanorobotic carrier demonstrate that the object arriving at a designated target is the same intact cargo that was originally loaded, that it was completely and correctly released, and that the carrier or its residues have been accounted for? This English-language research atlas converts cargo-delivery and micromanipulation demonstrations into a falsifiable end-to-end mission-integrity problem. The research develops a five-layer architecture for source identity and material tolerance, microscale contact mechanics, independently observable mission-state transitions, adversarial fault injection, and blind cross-platform requalification. Thirty mathematically distinct derivation stations connect probabilistic joint-task qualification to chemical mass balance, optical-label dissociation, surface adsorption, force-dependent detachment, microcontact mechanics, drag, kinetic release, spatial uncertainty, carryover contamination, whole-facility energy accounting, missing-fate bounds and hard safety vetoes. Eighty-two chapters each have a dedicated core-equation opening and five separate research sections. Two hundred Research Gates propose independent comparisons, physical perturbations, competing explanations, measurable failure criteria and reproducibility artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate systems that future investigators are invited to overturn, repair or rebuild. A machine-readable research atlas and formula-gate-DOI index enable AI-assisted comparison and future research reuse. The central endpoint is a correlated joint event: correct cargo identity and integrity, correct target, independently confirmed release, and verified carrier retrieval or authorized terminal disposition. The manuscript insists on counting every initiated mission rather than multiplying attractive substep success rates. It also distinguishes visible fluorescence from chemically intact cargo, externally actuated manipulation from on-board autonomy, and destination arrival from complete task closure. Strong benchmarks include optical tweezers, established magnetic-bead handling, microfluidic conveyance and conventional microgrippers under matched task difficulty, time and whole-facility energy use. Research status: This is a hypothesis-generating, nonclinical experimental-design atlas; it reports no newly conducted cargo experiments, clinical performance or proven integrated device. Foundational and recent DOI-identified publications provide engineering context but do not validate its new claims. The 200 Gates are open problems, not accomplished results. The actual text length and layout follow the substance of individual chapters rather than an artificially enforced 100,000-word count. items.summary: Analysis code and derived results for “Lineage-Restricted Reassortment and Glycoprotein Stability in Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus, 36 Countries, 1956–2025” This deposit contains the analysis code and the derived result files supporting the above manuscript (EID-26-1962, submitted to Emerging Infectious Diseases). The study assembled every publicly available Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) isolate for which the S, M and L genome segments were sequenced to near-completeness (429 isolates, 36 countries, 1956–2025), retrieved from GenBank, and asked whether segment reassortment is distributed evenly across the major lineages of the virus. The code reproduces: retrieval of the records from GenBank and assembly of the tri-segment isolate set; per-segment alignment (MAFFT) and maximum-likelihood phylogenies (FastTree 2, GTR+Γ); lineage and sublineage delimitation by clustering of pairwise p-distances; the sublineage-level test of intra-lineage segment exchange; simulation of the false-positive rate and of the probability that planted segment exchanges are detected; tests of the regional contrast at the level of independent ancestries under three counting rules and three definitions of lineage exposure; the amino-acid divergence analysis of the M-segment glycoprotein precursor by functional region; and the figures. No new sequence data are generated. All sequences analysed are publicly available in GenBank, and their accession numbers are listed in Appendix Table 1 of the manuscript. Contents: Python scripts ( *.py ), a README describing the run order and software requirements, and a results/ folder holding the output of every analysis in JSON so that the values reported in the manuscript text, tables and figures can be checked without re-running the pipeline. Requirements: Python 3 with numpy, scipy, biopython, matplotlib and openpyxl; MAFFT v7 and FastTree 2 on the path.

items.summary: AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND MISSION OBSERVABILITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation Research Flagship 01 | NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli This research atlas asks a difficult engineering question: when low-Reynolds-number microfluidic flows, Brownian orientation noise, boundary adhesion, external field actuation and incomplete sensing all influence a micro/nanorobot, what would justify calling its behavior autonomous navigation rather than externally assisted motion? The volume treats navigation as an auditable, bounded mission instead of an attractive trajectory. It develops a five-layer program spanning stochastic hydrodynamics, instrument and actuation provenance, uncertainty-calibrated belief-state estimation, blinded microfluidic challenges and independent requalification. Thirty linked mathematical stations differentiate physical relations, information-theoretic functionals and proposed navigation utility measures, with assumptions, dimensions and possible falsifiers. Eighty-two research chapters each open with a core mathematical relation, followed by five independent single-page research sections. Two hundred detailed Research Gates describe decisive comparisons, confounding explanations, evidence requirements, failure conditions and successor handoff artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos offer revisionable research prototypes rather than predetermined conclusions. The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. Foundational DOI-linked literature provides context, not proof of the proposed integrated system. Every major claim is designed to be revised, rejected or reconstructed by a successor team using raw evidence and pre-registered falsification rules. items.summary: We have presented a mathematically closed, comprehensive foundation for the C861 discrete spectral benchmark. By establishing the exact rank-two projector geometry, resolving Dirichlet sum cancellations, providing constructive proofs for linear B-spline KAN operator reproduction, and formalizing the Lyapunov convergence of Dense Associative Memory on spherical manifolds, this framework eliminates ambiguities in evaluating learned physical operators. Furthermore, the spectral interlacing analysis of the CN → PN structural homotopy equips the scientific machine learning community with a tool to distinguish authentic topological sensitivity from numerical discretization artifacts.
items.title: Exact Discrete Spectral Invariants as a Falsification Baseline for Learned Operator

items.summary: Agentic frameworks, software libraries that coordinate large language model calls, tool use, memory, and multi step reasoning into autonomous or semi autonomous workflows, have moved from research prototypes to production infrastructure within a span of roughly two years. Four frameworks have emerged as leading options for enterprise adoption: LangGraph, a graph based orchestration library built around explicit state machines, CrewAI, a role based framework that models agents as a crew of collaborating specialists, Strands Agents, a model driven software development kit that emphasizes minimal orchestration code, and watsonx Orchestrate, a managed enterprise platform built around prepackaged skills and governance tooling. Despite rapid adoption, there has been little independent, head to head measurement of how these frameworks compare on the dimensions that matter most to enterprise adopters: end to end latency, latency under concurrent load, cost per task, reliability and error recovery, and enterprise readiness characteristics such as security, observability, and governance. This article presents an empirical benchmark of all four frameworks against a common task suite spanning six task categories and three complexity tiers. We report latency percentiles, a stage level latency breakdown, concurrency scaling behavior, cost per task, task success rates, and a structured enterprise readiness score. We further document each framework's orchestration topology, developer experience characteristics, and security and governance posture, and we translate the results into a practical decision framework for selecting among the four frameworks under different enterprise constraints. All benchmark figures in this article are illustrative, reflecting a representative test harness and reference workload rather than any single vendor's published numbers, and are intended to demonstrate a repeatable evaluation method rather than a definitive ranking.
items.title: LANGGRAPH, CREWAI, STRANDS, OR WATSONX ORCHESTRATE? AN EMPIRICAL BENCHMARK OF AGENTIC FRAMEWORKS FOR ENTERPRISE READINESS AND LATENCY

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.
items.title: Inverse Radius Kernel and Optical Phase Registration

items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.
items.title: Fisher information metric tensors for 'Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information'

items.summary: This metadata entry record constitutes the fourth, concluding installment of a foundational cosmological paper tetralogy (complementing the preceding works registered under DOI:10.5281/zenodo.22763071, DOI:10.5281/zenodo.23153625, and DOI:10.5281/zenodo.23209528).  In this final paper, we formalize the self-consistent microphysical scenarios and underlying relativistic field equations governing primordial lepto- and baryogenesis within a strictly deterministic, parameter-free Extremal Quantum Black Hole (EQBH) cosmological bounce framework occurring immediately post-turnaround. Operating within the rigid geometric boundaries of an effective N=1 supergravity (SUGRA) action and a q-deformed U_q(su(2)) horizon algebra, we trace the top-down reverse-engineering map from Planck-scale remnants to Standard Model matter fields without invoking highly tuned auxiliary fields or unconstrained post-bounce inflation boundaries. items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

items.summary: This working paper develops a relational Phase interpretation of black holes within the Harmonic Physics research programme, using general relativity, exact Kerr geometry and semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics as its physical baseline. It examines how phase organisation, temporal reference, observer accessibility and information persistence might relate to black-hole closure. Within the proposed framework, a phase-cycle is a closed relational structure that supports recurrence. Measured succession requires distinguishable relations and persistent records, while geometry and causal history are treated as observer-level reconstructions. The temporal-anchor hypothesis concerns a deeper terminal condition at which the parent domain loses the internally usable references needed to resolve further clocks and geometry. This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. These results establish compatibility within the stated geometric constructions. A physical transition mechanism remains to be derived. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The remaining requirements include an invariant parent-relative terminal criterion, a physical Phase-to-boundary map, transition dynamics, information and entropy accounting, and a stable nonperturbative rotating completion. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. It does not establish a physical black-to-white transition, information recovery through evaporation or a daughter universe. Version 2.3, dated 17 October 2026, updates observation and self-nesting terminology, clarifies geodesic incompleteness and fixed-angular-momentum assumptions, and refreshes the references. The existing displayed equations and reported test results are retained. keywords: Phase Theory; black holes; event horizons; geodesic incompleteness; relational time; phase contraction; information accessibility; singularity; white holes; quantum gravity.

items.summary: Background: Long-segment intramedullary cervical cord lesions can present a diagnostic challenge, particularly when imaging findings raise suspicion of an intramedullary neoplasm. Differentiating a syrinx from an intramedullary tumor is important for operative planning, as the surgical strategy may differ substantially. Case presentation: A 43-year-old female presented with a six-month history of progressive cervical pain with radicular symptoms, vertigo, left upper-limb sensory disturbance, and impaired left-hand grip. Neurological examination revealed preserved motor power of 5/5 in all four limbs, normal reflexes, and reduced functional grip in the left hand. MRI of the cervical spine demonstrated a long-segment expansile intramedullary lesion extending from the cervicomedullary junction to C7, without contrast enhancement. The radiological report also described Chiari malformation and syringomyelia. Given the diagnostic uncertainty and progressive symptoms, we performed urgent surgical exploration within two days of admission. We performed a C3–C7 laminoplasty to provide multilevel posterior access while preserving the laminar elements without instrumented fixation. Following durotomy and midline myelotomy, a syrinx was identified, with no obvious intramedullary tumor. Syringotomy and drainage were performed, and adjacent spinal cord tissue was obtained for biopsy. Graft duraplasty and reconstruction of the elevated laminae were completed. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course, with relief of pain and vertigo and resolution of sensory symptoms. She was discharged with intact motor power and improved but residual left-hand grip weakness. Follow-up MRI demonstrated cord decompression and drainage of the syrinx. Conclusion: This case illustrates the diagnostic uncertainty that may arise when a long-segment non-enhancing intramedullary cervical lesion is suspected to represent a tumor. Intraoperative findings guided the surgical procedure toward syringotomy and drainage, with tissue sampling to investigate a possible underlying neoplasm. Multilevel laminoplasty provided posterior access while allowing reconstruction of the cervical laminar elements. Histopathological confirmation and longer-term follow-up remain necessary.

items.summary: Експертна методика визначає стадії та операції дослідження, однак сама їх послідовність іще не пояснює, за яких умов результатом однієї операції можна скористатися в наступній. У судовій гірничотехнічній експертизі найбільш відповідальними є переходи від відомостей, що їх містять матеріали, до реконструкції механізму події, від реконструкції – до оцінювання причинного значення обставин, а від установленої дії або бездіяльності – до її технічного співвіднесення з функціями конкретної особи. Мета роботи полягає у формуванні критеріїв, за якими придатність проміжного результату перевіряють до його застосування в наступній операції, та у з’ясуванні зв’язку між фактичною основою – сукупністю достатніх, узгоджених і простежуваних відомостей – і допустимими межами підсумкової відповіді експерта. Дослідження поєднало структурне моделювання, формально-логічний аналіз експертного міркування, зіставлення з положеннями судової експертології та теоретико-методичне узагальнення професійного досвіду у сфері судової гірничотехнічної експертизи. Застосування моделі проілюстровано на двох знеособлених типізованих ситуаціях із завершеної експертної практики 2015–2023 років, що відображають різний стан фактичної основи. Обґрунтовано поняття критерію контрольованого переходу й сім функціональних контрольних точок: відповідності питання компетенції експерта; достатності матеріалів; узгодженості та простежуваності відомостей; можливості реконструкції механізму; причинного значення обставин; суб’єктно-функціонального співвіднесення; синтезу й оцінювання результатів. Для фіксації методичного рішення запропоновано статуси контрольованого переходу: Т+ – дозволений перехід, Т± – обмежено дозволений перехід, Т– – недозволений перехід. Практичними результатами є модель проходження контрольної точки, матриця методичних рішень і структура робочої карти, придатні для використання як методичний модуль судової гірничотехнічної експертизи. Застосування критеріїв контрольованого переходу пов’язує стан фактичної основи з допустимим напрямом подальшого аналізу й запобігає формулюванню відповіді поза обумовленими межами.

items.summary: AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND MISSION OBSERVABILITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation Research Flagship 01 | NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli This research atlas asks a difficult engineering question: when low-Reynolds-number microfluidic flows, Brownian orientation noise, boundary adhesion, external field actuation and incomplete sensing all influence a micro/nanorobot, what would justify calling its behavior autonomous navigation rather than externally assisted motion? The volume treats navigation as an auditable, bounded mission instead of an attractive trajectory. It develops a five-layer program spanning stochastic hydrodynamics, instrument and actuation provenance, uncertainty-calibrated belief-state estimation, blinded microfluidic challenges and independent requalification. Thirty linked mathematical stations differentiate physical relations, information-theoretic functionals and proposed navigation utility measures, with assumptions, dimensions and possible falsifiers. Eighty-two research chapters each open with a core mathematical relation, followed by five independent single-page research sections. Two hundred detailed Research Gates describe decisive comparisons, confounding explanations, evidence requirements, failure conditions and successor handoff artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos offer revisionable research prototypes rather than predetermined conclusions. The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. Foundational DOI-linked literature provides context, not proof of the proposed integrated system. Every major claim is designed to be revised, rejected or reconstructed by a successor team using raw evidence and pre-registered falsification rules. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. This version preserves the v5.1 derived results and adds a claim-to-evidence map, measurement source, pinned dependency identities, configurations, setup guidance and six complete sanitized scientific run records. items.summary: NANOROBOTIC CARGO TRANSPORT AND MICROSCALE MANIPULATION INTEGRITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation DOI Fission Research Flagship 02 | Starli Active Nanosystems Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli | Research Atlas v1.0 (October 2026) How can a micro/nanorobotic carrier demonstrate that the object arriving at a designated target is the same intact cargo that was originally loaded, that it was completely and correctly released, and that the carrier or its residues have been accounted for? This English-language research atlas converts cargo-delivery and micromanipulation demonstrations into a falsifiable end-to-end mission-integrity problem. The research develops a five-layer architecture for source identity and material tolerance, microscale contact mechanics, independently observable mission-state transitions, adversarial fault injection, and blind cross-platform requalification. Thirty mathematically distinct derivation stations connect probabilistic joint-task qualification to chemical mass balance, optical-label dissociation, surface adsorption, force-dependent detachment, microcontact mechanics, drag, kinetic release, spatial uncertainty, carryover contamination, whole-facility energy accounting, missing-fate bounds and hard safety vetoes. Eighty-two chapters each have a dedicated core-equation opening and five separate research sections. Two hundred Research Gates propose independent comparisons, physical perturbations, competing explanations, measurable failure criteria and reproducibility artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate systems that future investigators are invited to overturn, repair or rebuild. A machine-readable research atlas and formula-gate-DOI index enable AI-assisted comparison and future research reuse. The central endpoint is a correlated joint event: correct cargo identity and integrity, correct target, independently confirmed release, and verified carrier retrieval or authorized terminal disposition. The manuscript insists on counting every initiated mission rather than multiplying attractive substep success rates. It also distinguishes visible fluorescence from chemically intact cargo, externally actuated manipulation from on-board autonomy, and destination arrival from complete task closure. Strong benchmarks include optical tweezers, established magnetic-bead handling, microfluidic conveyance and conventional microgrippers under matched task difficulty, time and whole-facility energy use. Research status: This is a hypothesis-generating, nonclinical experimental-design atlas; it reports no newly conducted cargo experiments, clinical performance or proven integrated device. Foundational and recent DOI-identified publications provide engineering context but do not validate its new claims. The 200 Gates are open problems, not accomplished results. The actual text length and layout follow the substance of individual chapters rather than an artificially enforced 100,000-word count. items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol). We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.
items.title: Drivers of LLM Consensus Formation Under Competing Incentives: A Simulation Study

items.summary: EHR2Trace converts local hospital EHR extracts (delimited text and spreadsheets) into OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS. items.summary: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. We propose PRB-WM, a physics-regularized Beta world model for predictive per-subcarrier link adaptation on real time-varying UWA channels. A persistence-anchored stochastic latent-space dynamics model learns how the channel evolves; a counterfactual outcome head evaluates, for every candidate modulation and coding scheme (MCS), a Beta-binomial distribution of bit errors on shared imagined futures; and a chance-constrained receding-horizon model predictive controller maximizes expected spectral efficiency subject to a bounded probability of violating the bit error rate (BER) target. To the best of our knowledge, PRB-WM is the first world model for UWA communications. In closed-loop replay of six measured sea-trial links from the public UWA Channel Library against a 24-method pool spanning the full methodological spectrum, PRB-WM attains a mean goodput 87% above the strongest baseline, ranks first on all six time-varying links at the longest lookahead, and is the only method whose realized frame risk decreases systematically with lookahead, meeting the BER-violation contract where no baseline does. Ablations confirm that rollout sampling dispersion is essential to the chance constraint and that the physics anchor is necessary for trainability.
items.title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels

items.summary: AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND MISSION OBSERVABILITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation Research Flagship 01 | NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli This research atlas asks a difficult engineering question: when low-Reynolds-number microfluidic flows, Brownian orientation noise, boundary adhesion, external field actuation and incomplete sensing all influence a micro/nanorobot, what would justify calling its behavior autonomous navigation rather than externally assisted motion? The volume treats navigation as an auditable, bounded mission instead of an attractive trajectory. It develops a five-layer program spanning stochastic hydrodynamics, instrument and actuation provenance, uncertainty-calibrated belief-state estimation, blinded microfluidic challenges and independent requalification. Thirty linked mathematical stations differentiate physical relations, information-theoretic functionals and proposed navigation utility measures, with assumptions, dimensions and possible falsifiers. Eighty-two research chapters each open with a core mathematical relation, followed by five independent single-page research sections. Two hundred detailed Research Gates describe decisive comparisons, confounding explanations, evidence requirements, failure conditions and successor handoff artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos offer revisionable research prototypes rather than predetermined conclusions. The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. Foundational DOI-linked literature provides context, not proof of the proposed integrated system. Every major claim is designed to be revised, rejected or reconstructed by a successor team using raw evidence and pre-registered falsification rules. items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23431625 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes The introduction clearly explains the research objectives. It states that the study aims to replicate the quantitative analysis of Krause, Krause, and Bränfors (2018), assess the reproducibility of their findings, and examine potential limitations concerning statistical power and model specification. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate The replication approach is suitable for the research, as the authors reproduce the original Cox proportional hazards models and robustness tests. However, the methodological assessment has some gaps. In particular, the power analysis reports values of 0.44 and 0.99 without providing the formula, software procedure, or sufficient calculation details to allow readers to reproduce the estimates. The choice of 42 events in Table 6 also needs clarification, given that Table 5 reports 54 events overall. Additionally, the differences between the original and reproduced sample sizes remain unexplained. These issues weaken the transparency and reproducibility of the analysis. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported The main conclusion is that the original findings can be reproduced, which is supported by the reported results. The authors also reasonably identify the small number of female-signatory agreements and the limitations of drawing causal conclusions from the observed association. However, the claim that the analysis has low statistical power relies on a calculation for which the formula and detailed procedure are not provided (Table 6). The differences between the original and reproduced sample sizes also remain unexplained. These limitations make some aspects of the interpretation less conclusive than they could be. Are the data presentations, including visualizations, well-suited to represent the data? Somewhat appropriate and clear The survival analysis and regression tables are suitable for presenting the findings. However, some numerical inconsistencies in the descriptive statistics and differences in sample sizes across the original and reproduced models need clarification to ensure the results are presented accurately. For instance, Table 3 presents: three major statistical flaws: 1: Conflict Intensity row, where Female Signatories = 1: has SD of 1.2 while the Max is 0.45, which is statistically incorrect. Similarly, (2) Democracy row where Female Signatories = 1, has Mean 0.92 < Min 1. And lastly, on page 5, UN peacekeeping is written as a binary number, however, in Table 3, the binary UN Peacekeeping has Max > 1. All these minor inconsistencies require clarification. How clearly do the authors discuss, explain, and interpret their findings and potential next steps for the research? Very clearly The authors explain their findings, acknowledge the limitations of the small number of agreements with female signatories, and discuss the implications for causal interpretation. They also identify the need for further research, although the power analysis and differences in sample sizes could be explained more transparently. Is the preprint likely to advance academic knowledge? Somewhat likely If the author clarified the sample-size discrepancies and documented the power analysis more transparently, then it would substantially contribute to the reproducibility of an influential finding, as it already highlights the reproducibility of the findings and highlights the limitations in statistical power and causal interpretation. Package Contents: data/: Anonymized benchmark dataset (students_data_tesis_final.csv) featuring 168-hour weekly availability matrices and raw ablation output. benchmarks/: Automated Python scripts for Stratified 5-fold cross-validation ablation (C1 to C4), Wilcoxon Signed-Rank hypothesis testing, Cliff's Delta effect size calculation, and bootstrap confidence intervals. database/: PostgreSQL 16 schema and stored procedure definitions for HNSW Approximate Nearest Neighbor vector search (pgvector) and dynamic schedule intersection. turborepo-src/: Clean source code of the decoupled microservices monorepo (API Gateway, Matching Service, ML Engine, and shared Protocol Buffers). System Requirements: Python 3.10+ with NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, and NLTK. Node.js v20+ / pnpm v9+ and Docker Engine for microservice orchestration.

items.summary: Python code that reproduces all results, figures and supporting tables of Dixit, AchutaRao and Sandeep, "Future Warming Shortens the Memory of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and Erodes a Source of Near-Term Predictability" (submitted to Earth's Future). The analysis uses eleven CMIP6 models (piControl, historical, SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5), the CESM2 and MIROC6 large ensembles and ERSSTv5, regridded to the 2-degree ERSSTv5 grid. "bash run_all.sh" runs the full analysis. The folder results/ contains the outputs used in the paper, from which most figures can be redrawn without the model data. See README.md for requirements, input data layout and the mapping of scripts to sections, figures and tables.
items.title: Code and results for "Future Warming Shortens the Memory of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and Erodes a Source of Near-Term Predictability"

items.summary: Code, trained networks and data for the paper “Physics-informed neural networks for maximizing quantum Fisher information in time-dependent many-body systems”. The archive Zenodo_deposit.zip is self-contained. It holds the training method (a counter-diabatic control expanded in Pauli strings, with a learned schedule, propagated with a fourth-order commutator-free Magnus integrator), the trained network and configuration of every reported run, Supplementary Data 1 (source data of every figure and table), Supplementary Data 2 (pulse files), and a script that regenerates the figures, tables and reported numbers and checks them against the deposited values. Instructions are in README.md inside the archive. Version 2.0.6 re-exports the figure PDFs of the archive; the code, trained networks and data are those of version 2.0.5. Version 2.0.5 corrects the description of the QFI floor and of the stored candidates in the README so that it matches the code, redraws Supplementary Fig. 1 with a key grouped by kind of control, and adds the panels of the time-resolved QFI to Supplementary Fig. 4; the trained networks and data are those of version 2.0.4. Version 2.0.4 completes the regeneration path of the Supplementary Information: python reproduce.py baselines covers every size computed in the paper (ideal control up to twelve qubits), python reproduce.py symmetry also reports the symmetry fractions and compares the Holm-corrected p-values and partial correlations, python reproduce.py verify --exact repeats the dense validation, python reproduce.py replay retrains a paper run against its stored history, and the three runs of the propagation-cadence calibration are included (983 runs). The README documents the selection rules and step control as implemented. Supplementary Data 1 no longer lists the unreported right-limit probe rows of exact_controls.csv ; the trained networks and all other data are unchanged. Download: the archive is stored in eleven parts. Rejoin them with cat Zenodo_deposit.zip.part-* > Zenodo_deposit.zip (on Windows, copy /b Zenodo_deposit.zip.part-aa + Zenodo_deposit.zip.part-ab + ... Zenodo_deposit.zip , listing the parts in order) and check the result with shasum -a 256 -c Zenodo_deposit.zip.sha256 . License: the code is released under the MIT License, and the data, trained networks, figures and tables under CC BY 4.0. Preprint of the first version of the manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18506

items.summary: AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND MISSION OBSERVABILITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation Research Flagship 01 | NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli This research atlas asks a difficult engineering question: when low-Reynolds-number microfluidic flows, Brownian orientation noise, boundary adhesion, external field actuation and incomplete sensing all influence a micro/nanorobot, what would justify calling its behavior autonomous navigation rather than externally assisted motion? The volume treats navigation as an auditable, bounded mission instead of an attractive trajectory. It develops a five-layer program spanning stochastic hydrodynamics, instrument and actuation provenance, uncertainty-calibrated belief-state estimation, blinded microfluidic challenges and independent requalification. Thirty linked mathematical stations differentiate physical relations, information-theoretic functionals and proposed navigation utility measures, with assumptions, dimensions and possible falsifiers. Eighty-two research chapters each open with a core mathematical relation, followed by five independent single-page research sections. Two hundred detailed Research Gates describe decisive comparisons, confounding explanations, evidence requirements, failure conditions and successor handoff artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos offer revisionable research prototypes rather than predetermined conclusions. The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. Foundational DOI-linked literature provides context, not proof of the proposed integrated system. Every major claim is designed to be revised, rejected or reconstructed by a successor team using raw evidence and pre-registered falsification rules. PARENT RESEARCH DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23046134 Original parent: NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE AT THE LIMIT. Parent-chapter lineage: Ch. 06-11 (navigation), 47-51 (estimation/control), 65 and 68 (benchmarking and transfer). The current child manuscript does not yet have an independent DOI; one would be assigned only upon actual repository deposit. Editorial release note: the manuscript prioritizes non-duplicative research content and independent testability over an artificial word-count target. It is suitable as a research architecture for additional scientific review, not a substitute for physical validation.

items.summary: Companion code for the preprint "Benchmarking Real-Time DETR Detectors for Multibeam Forward-Looking Sonar: DEIMv2, Detector-Specific Test-Time Fusion, and Domain Shift Analysis on UATD" (Preprints 2026, 2026090449, doi:10.20944/preprints202609.0449.v3). Contains the DEIMv2 engine with UATD configs, the TTA/WBF fusion tooling (default --wbf-rule view-dedup; query-level retained as reproduction control), the paired image-level bootstrap CI scripts, the paper's three central results tables as CSV, and unit tests pinning the WBF view-dedup rule and the bootstrap identity property. The UATD dataset itself is NOT redistributed; fetch it from the official figshare channel (article 21331143) via the included download scripts. License: benchmark code MIT; the DEIMv2 engine remains under the DEIMv2 non-commercial license (LICENSE-DEIMv2.md). v3 (2026-09-29): reviewer-comment C13 fix — analysis/bootstrap_ci.py now averages AR@100 over valid recall entries only (excluding the -1 sentinel for classes absent from a bootstrap resample), matching the COCOeval convention already used for mAP. Adds analysis/bootstrap_arfix_recompute.py (analytic recompute of all 14 archived AR@100 bootstrap intervals from the per-replicate CSVs), results/boot_out/*_arfixed.json (defective-vs-fixed intervals; max change 0.001 on any bound, no reported number changes), and tests/test_bootstrap_missing_class.py pinning the fixed behavior. v4 (2026-10-17): adds the DEIMv2-S seed-43/44 fusion summary ( results/ablation_wbf_dedup_seed4344_summary.json ) with its generation script ( tools/ablation_wbf_dedup_seed4344.py ) and the run log ( results/S_seed4344_fusion_20261014.md ), as referenced in the paper's Table II note; README updated (preprint v3 DOI, 90/10 seed-42 split reproduction command, seed-43/44 result registration, and a note cross-checking the vendored WBF against the reference PyPI package ensemble-boxes 1.0.6); manifests regenerated (252 files). v5 (2026-10-18): adds the score-only control ablation for the view-deduplication analysis (paper Sec. III-B): generation script ( tools/ablation_scoreonly_test1.py ) and results ( results/ablation_scoreonly_test1.json , Test_1: query-level vs score-only vs view-dedup, isolating score normalization from member removal); README updated (tool and result registration); manifests regenerated (254 files). The preprint reference remains doi:10.20944/preprints202609.0449.v3.

items.summary: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. We propose PRB-WM, a physics-regularized Beta world model for predictive per-subcarrier link adaptation on real time-varying UWA channels. A persistence-anchored stochastic latent-space dynamics model learns how the channel evolves; a counterfactual outcome head evaluates, for every candidate modulation and coding scheme (MCS), a Beta-binomial distribution of bit errors on shared imagined futures; and a chance-constrained receding-horizon model predictive controller maximizes expected spectral efficiency subject to a bounded probability of violating the bit error rate (BER) target. To the best of our knowledge, PRB-WM is the first world model for UWA communications. In closed-loop replay of six measured sea-trial links from the public UWA Channel Library against a 24-method pool spanning the full methodological spectrum, PRB-WM attains a mean goodput 87% above the strongest baseline, ranks first on all six time-varying links at the longest lookahead, and is the only method whose realized frame risk decreases systematically with lookahead, meeting the BER-violation contract where no baseline does. Ablations confirm that rollout sampling dispersion is essential to the chance constraint and that the physics anchor is necessary for trainability.
items.title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels
